summary: For every i from 1 to N we take its digit sum and raise it to the number of digits, then add all those values (T2 — digits, inside a T1 loop). N is small enough that the direct loop is fast.

blocks.title: Digit sum and digit count
blocks.text: `str(i)` gives the digits as text. Summing `int(d)` gives the digit sum `S`, and `len` gives the digit count `D`.

blocks.title: Raise and add
blocks.text: `**` is the power operator. `^` in Python is XOR, which gives a completely different number.

blocks.title: Print the answer
blocks.text: Exact format: `Total sum: 434`. Python handles the 13-digit total for N = 100,000.

complexity: Time O(N · digits) with N ≤ 100,000 → about 600,000 digit operations (~0.13 s).
